title: Vectors in Depth — Geometry, Lines & Applications
subject: maths

questions.feedbackWrong: Subtracting a negative x-component: $6 - (-1) = 7$, and $-4 - 5 = -9$ — so $7\mathbf{i} - 9\mathbf{j}$.

mistakes.misconception: Subtracts the negative x-component as if adding a negative — sign error.
mistakes.correction: $2\mathbf{a} - \mathbf{b}$ means $6 - (-1)$ for the i-component: subtracting a negative ADDS.

questions.prompt: Vectors $\mathbf{a} = \mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j}$ and $\mathbf{b} = 3\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j}$. Compute the dot product $\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}$.
Explain the meaning of each part of the vector equation of a line $\mathbf{r} = \mathbf{a} + t\mathbf{d}$, and describe how you would find where two such lines intersect.

markScheme.text: $\mathbf{a}$ is the position vector of a fixed point ON the line.
$\mathbf{d}$ is the direction vector; t is a scalar parameter ranging over all reals — each t gives one point.
For intersection: set the two equations equal with DIFFERENT parameters (e.g. t and s) since the point may occur at different parameter values.
Equate i and j components for simultaneous equations in s and t, solve, and substitute back — checking consistency.

mistakes.misconception: Uses one parameter t for both lines when finding intersections.
mistakes.correction: The lines are independent — the intersection point generally corresponds to different parameter values on each, so you need t AND s.

questions.feedbackCorrect: Correct — $2\mathbf{i} - 3\mathbf{j}$ is exactly half, a scalar multiple.

mistakes.correction: Both components must scale by the SAME factor including sign — flipping one sign changes direction.

questions.prompt: In triangle OAB, M is the midpoint of AB. Using vectors, prove that $\overrightarrow{OM} = \frac{1}{2}(\mathbf{a} + \mathbf{b})$ where $\mathbf{a}$, $\mathbf{b}$ are the position vectors of A and B.
questions.guidance: Write the journey O to M via A.

markScheme.text: $= \mathbf{a} - \frac{1}{2}\mathbf{a} + \frac{1}{2}\mathbf{b} = \frac{1}{2}(\mathbf{a} + \mathbf{b})$ as required — a proof, not verification.

questions.prompt: Find the magnitude of the unit vector in the direction of $6\mathbf{i} + 8\mathbf{j}$ — i.e. the magnitude OF that unit vector (a trivial check), then the x-component of the unit vector as a decimal.
Points A, B, C are collinear. If $\overrightarrow{AB} = 2\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j}$, which could be $\overrightarrow{BC}$?
questions.feedbackCorrect: Correct — $\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j} = \frac{1}{2}\overrightarrow{AB}$, a scalar multiple, so the points lie on one straight line.
questions.feedbackWrong: Collinear means the segments share a direction — $\overrightarrow{BC}$ must be a scalar multiple of $\overrightarrow{AB}$: only $\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j}$ is.

mistakes.correction: Collinearity is about direction, not length — only scalar multiples preserve direction.

questions.prompt: A point P has position vector $2\mathbf{i} - 3\mathbf{j} + 4\mathbf{k}$. Describe how to find its distance from the origin and compute it exactly in surd form.

markScheme.text: Distance from origin = magnitude of the position vector (3D Pythagoras).
